text:
Race condition. Multiple requests read same value before any write commit.

## Problem

```
Request A: READ counter (5) ──┐
Request B: READ counter (5) ──┤  both read 5
Request A: WRITE 5+1 = 6    ──┤
Request B: WRITE 5+1 = 6    ──┘  both write 6, one increment lost
```

## Fix Options

### 1. Atomic UPDATE (best, simplest)

```sql
UPDATE counters
SET value = value + 1
WHERE id = $1
RETURNING value;
```

DB handle increment atomically. No read-then-write in app. One query.

### 2. SELECT FOR UPDATE (need transaction, more control)

```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT value FROM counters WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE;
-- row locked, other requests block here
UPDATE counters SET value = value + 1 WHERE id = $1 RETURNING value;
COMMIT;
```

Use when increment logic complex (not just +1).

### 3. Node.js code

```js
// BAD - race condition
const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE id = $1', [id]);
await pool.query('UPDATE counters SET value = $1 WHERE id = $2', [rows[0].value + 1, id]);

// GOOD - atomic
const { rows } = await pool.query(
  'UPDATE counters SET value = value + 1 WHERE id = $1 RETURNING value',
  [id]
);
return rows[0].value;
```

## Pick one

| Situation | Fix |
|-----------|-----|
| Simple increment | Atomic `UPDATE` |
| Complex logic on value | `SELECT FOR UPDATE` in transaction |
| Need "compare and swap" | Optimistic lock + retry loop |

Atomic UPDATE cover 95% of cases. Use that.
